# Email rules by country

**This is not legal advice.** This page is a summary of public sources for the tool's checklist. Laws change and courts read them differently. If you are unsure, ask a lawyer before you send.

Last researched: 2026-10-14. Rows older than six months should be checked again.

LinkedIn is separate. These rules cover email only. Lead Generator never logs in to LinkedIn or sends LinkedIn messages. If you send LinkedIn messages with another tool, read LinkedIn's User Agreement and its rules on automation first.

## Do not send without documented consent

### Australia (AU)

- **Law:** Spam Act 2003 (Cth), enforced by ACMA
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Australia requires consent before sending commercial email, but consent can be inferred from a work address that is conspicuously published (and not marked as no-spam) when your message relates to the person's role. Every message needs accurate sender identity and a working unsubscribe that is processed within 5 working days. Addresses guessed from a name pattern do not qualify, so record your basis for each recipient. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.legislation.gov.au/C2004A01214/2016-03-10/2016-03-10/text/original/pdf; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=AU

### Austria (AT)

- **Law:** Telecommunications Act 2021 (TKG) section 174; GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Austria prohibits email for direct marketing without the recipient's prior consent, and the government reads this as covering business recipients too; the exception is for your own customers and similar products with an easy opt-out. Do not send cold email to Austria without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.ris.bka.gv.at/eli/bgbl/i/2021/190/P174/NOR40238632; https://www.bmf.gv.at/en/topics/Telecom-and-Postal-Services/Telecommunications-Law-and-Policy/Unsolicited-messages.html; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=AT; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Canada (CA)

- **Law:** Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation (CASL, S.C. 2010, c. 23)
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include your postal address, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Canada requires consent before commercial email. Consent is implied only in narrow cases, such as a recent customer or enquiry, or an address the person conspicuously published (without a no-unsolicited-messages notice) where your message is relevant to their role. Messages must identify you, include a mailing address and a working unsubscribe honoured within 10 business days, and you must be able to prove consent; guessed addresses do not qualify. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/E-1.6/FullText.html; https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/canada-anti-spam-legislation/en/node/7; https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/acts/C-34/section-52.01.html

### China (CN)

- **Law:** Measures for the Administration of Internet E-mail Services (2006); Personal Information Protection Law
- **Consent model:** opt in
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful, label the subject line (label: `AD`)
- **In plain English:** China requires the recipient's explicit consent for marketing email. Each message must identify the sender and carry the mark 广告 or AD in the subject. Do not send cold email to recipients in China without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=CN

### Denmark (DK)

- **Law:** Marketing Practices Act (Danish); GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Denmark requires the recipient's prior consent for marketing email, and the ban covers business recipients as well as consumers. The only business carve-out is narrow and applies to an existing customer relationship with an easy opt-out. Never conceal the sender. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.danskerhverv.dk/presse-og-nyheder/nyheder/2018/august/samtykke-til-markedsforing/; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=DK; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Germany (DE)

- **Law:** Act Against Unfair Competition (UWG) section 7; ePrivacy Directive Art. 13; GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Germany treats email advertising without the recipient's prior express consent as an unacceptable nuisance, and this applies to business recipients too; the only exception is for your own customers whose address you got through a sale. Concealing the sender or having no valid opt-out address is also unlawful. Do not send cold email to Germany without documented consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/englisch_uwg/englisch_uwg.html; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Italy (IT)

- **Law:** Privacy Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003) section 130; GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Italy requires prior informed consent (opt-in) for marketing email, recorded with its date, and the rule covers business recipients as well as individuals. There is a soft exception for existing customers and similar products. Include a simple way to opt out in every message. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=IT; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Japan (JP)

- **Law:** Act on Regulation of Transmission of Specified Electronic Mail (Act 26 of 2002); Act on Specified Commercial Transactions
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include your postal address, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Japan requires prior consent for advertising email, with exceptions for people who gave you their address (for example a business card), people you already do business with, and businesses that publicly disclosed their address. Each email must show the sender's name and address and an opt-out address, and you must stop once someone refuses. Addresses guessed from a pattern do not qualify. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.soumu.go.jp/main_sosiki/joho_tsusin/eng/Resources/laws/Specified-E-mail-index.pdf; https://monolith.law/en/it/e-mail-newsletter-opt-in-procedure; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=JP

### Netherlands (NL)

- **Law:** Telecommunicatiewet (Telecommunications Act) Art. 11.7; GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** The Netherlands bans unsolicited commercial email unless the sender can show prior consent. Business recipients are exempt only if they published the address for the purpose of receiving such messages, so a guessed or scraped work address does not qualify. Offer a free opt-out and keep proof of consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0009950/; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### New Zealand (NZ)

- **Law:** Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** New Zealand requires express, inferred or deemed consent before commercial email. Deemed consent applies when someone conspicuously publishes a work address (without a no-unsolicited-messages notice) and your message relates to their role. Every message must identify the sender and have a free unsubscribe honoured within five working days; addresses guessed from a pattern do not qualify. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dia.govt.nz/Spam-Three-Steps; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=NZ

### Poland (PL)

- **Law:** Electronic Communications Act Art. 398; GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Poland prohibits sending unsolicited commercial information, including direct marketing, to a subscriber or end user by telecommunication equipment without prior consent, and the rule is not limited to consumers. Consent must be explicit and cannot be pre-ticked. Do not send cold email to Poland without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=PL; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Qatar (QA)

- **Law:** Personal Data Privacy Protection Law (Law 13 of 2016)
- **Consent model:** opt in
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Qatar requires prior, explicit consent before sending electronic marketing. Every message must show who sent it, say that it is direct marketing, give a reachable address and let the recipient withdraw consent at any time. Do not send cold email to Qatar without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=QA

### South Africa (ZA)

- **Law:** Protection of Personal Information Act 2013 (POPIA) section 69
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** South Africa prohibits direct marketing by email unless the person has consented or is your customer; this covers companies as well as individuals. You may approach someone only once to ask for consent, in the prescribed form, and customers must be offered a free opt-out each time. Do not send cold email to South Africa without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://popia.co.za/section-69-direct-marketing-by-means-of-unsolicited-electronic-communications/; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=ZA

### South Korea (KR)

- **Law:** Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection (Network Act) Art. 50
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** South Korea requires the recipient's explicit prior consent before commercial electronic advertising is sent, with a limited exception for your own recent customers. The message must show who you are and how to refuse, and you must stop after a refusal. Korean rules may also require a marking in the subject line that was not verified here, so check before sending. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=KR

### Spain (ES)

- **Law:** Law 34/2002 (LSSI) Art. 20-21; GDPR and LOPDGDD
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Spain prohibits advertising email that the recipient has not requested or expressly authorised, and the rule covers business recipients too; the exception is for existing customers and similar products. Messages must be clearly identifiable as commercial, name the sender and include a valid address for opting out. Do not send cold email to Spain without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.boe.es/buscar/act.php?id=BOE-A-2002-13758; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=ES; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Switzerland (CH)

- **Law:** Federal Act Against Unfair Competition (UCA) Art. 3(1)(o)
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include your postal address, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Switzerland requires prior consent for mass advertising by email, and the rule applies to business recipients as well as consumers; the only exception is for your own customers and similar products offered an easy opt-out. Messages must show your correct name, address and email contact and a free opt-out. Do not send cold email to Switzerland without consent. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=CH

### Vietnam (VN)

- **Law:** Decree 91/2020/ND-CP on anti-spam messages, emails and calls
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful, label the subject line (label: `[QC]`)
- **In plain English:** Vietnam allows advertising email only within tight rules: the advertiser must be identifiable, every email needs a working opt-out, the subject must start with [QC] (or [AD]), and you may not keep sending after a refusal (no more than three ads per day). Do not send cold advertising email to Vietnamese recipients without their agreement. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=VN; https://lawnet.vn/thong-tin-phap-luat/en/chinh-sach-moi/vietnam-05-advertising-email-requirements-115216.html

## Allowed with care (you must acknowledge a warning first)

### Belgium (BE)

- **Law:** Code of Economic Law Book XII (e-commerce); GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Belgium requires prior, informed consent for electronic marketing, with exceptions for existing customers and for messages to legal persons such as a general company address, both under strict conditions. Every message must say how to opt out and allow doing so electronically. Named personal addresses are also personal data. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=BE; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Brazil (BR)

- **Law:** General Data Protection Law (LGPD); Consumer Defence Code
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Brazil has no specific email marketing law; the data protection law needs a lawful basis (consent or legitimate interest) to use contact data, and you must stop when someone asks. Identify yourself, keep messages truthful and include an easy opt-out. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=BR

### Finland (FI)

- **Law:** Act on Electronic Communications Services; GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Finland requires prior consent for direct marketing email to individuals, but you may market to companies unless they have forbidden it. Everyone must be able to opt out easily and free of charge, and you must tell them how. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=FI; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### France (FR)

- **Law:** Postal and Electronic Communications Code Art. L. 34-5 (CNIL guidance); GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** France requires consent for consumers, but allows email to professionals about their own professional activity if they were told at collection that their address would be used for marketing and can object easily. Every message must name the advertiser and offer an opt-out. Generic company addresses are outside the consent rules. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=FR; https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2002/58/oj; https://prighter.com/resources/laws/eprivacy-directive/articles/article-13

### Hong Kong (HK)

- **Law:** Unsolicited Electronic Messages Ordinance (Cap. 593); Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Hong Kong lets you send commercial email without prior consent, but each message must carry accurate sender information and a working unsubscribe, subjects must not mislead, and you must stop once someone opts out. Using a named person's data for direct marketing also needs the notice and opt-out steps of the privacy ordinance. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.elegislation.gov.hk/hk/cap593; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=HK

### India (IN)

- **Law:** Information Technology Act 2000; Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** India has no anti-spam statute for email; telecom marketing rules cover calls and SMS, and the new data protection law lets people withdraw consent for marketing. Cold business email is not banned, but be accurate about who you are, include a working unsubscribe and stop when asked. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=IN

### Indonesia (ID)

- **Law:** Personal Data Protection Law (Law 27 of 2022)
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Indonesia has no dedicated email marketing law, but the data protection law needs a lawful basis (usually consent) to use someone's personal data and lets people withdraw consent. Treat business contact data carefully, identify yourself and honour unsubscribe requests straight away. This is not legal advice.

- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=ID

### Ireland (IE)

- **Law:** S.I. 336 of 2011 (ePrivacy Regulations); GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Ireland needs consent to market to individuals, but business-to-business email can generally be sent unless the recipient has said it does not consent. The sender must not be disguised and an opt-out must be offered. Breaches are criminal offences with fines per message, and named addresses are also personal data under GDPR. This is not legal advice.

### Kenya (KE)

- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Kenya allows personal data to be used for direct marketing only with consent, or where it was collected from the person, they were told about marketing and a simple opt-out exists with no opt-out request made. Data scraped from elsewhere does not fit this, so treat consent as the safer default and honour opt-outs. This is not legal advice.

- **In plain English:** Malaysia has no anti-spam rule in force for email yet; the Personal Data Protection Act lets people require you to stop using their data for direct marketing. The regulator has consulted on a rule needing consent and a free unsubscribe, so expect tightening. Identify yourself, add an unsubscribe line and stop immediately when asked. ### United Arab Emirates (AE)

- **Law:** TDRA Unsolicited Electronic Communications Regulation; Federal Decree-Law 45 of 2021 (PDPL); Federal Decree-Law 14 of 2023 (trading by modern technological means)
- **Consent model:** opt in with exceptions
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** The UAE has no single email marketing law. The telecoms regulator treats marketing sent without the recipient's consent as spam, the data protection law lets people stop direct marketing, and consumers can choose not to receive marketing email. Treat consent as the safer default, identify yourself and honour opt-outs. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=AE

### United Kingdom (GB)

- **Law:** Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations 2003 (PECR); UK GDPR
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** Companies and other corporate bodies can be emailed without prior consent, but sole traders and some partnerships count as individuals and need consent (or a soft opt-in for existing customers). Never hide who you are, give a valid address for opt-outs and keep a do-not-email list. Named addresses are also personal data under UK GDPR. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/electronic-mail-marketing/; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=GB

## Allowed if every email has a clear opt-out

### Singapore (SG)

- **Law:** Spam Control Act 2007 (bulk unsolicited commercial email); PDPA Do Not Call rules cover phone numbers only
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful, label the subject line (label: `<ADV>`)
- **In plain English:** Singapore does not require consent for unsolicited commercial email, but once you send in bulk (more than 100 similar messages in 24 hours, 1,000 in 30 days or 10,000 in a year) the subject must start with <ADV>, be truthful, and the message must carry an English unsubscribe statement with a working address that is honoured within 10 business days. This tool adds <ADV> and the unsubscribe line to every Singapore email to be safe. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://sso.agc.gov.sg/Act/SCA2007; https://www.dlapiperdataprotection.com/index.html?t=electronic-marketing&c=SG

### United States (US)

- **Law:** CAN-SPAM Act 2003 (15 U.S.C. 7701 ff.), enforced by the FTC
- **Consent model:** opt out
- **Every email must:** say who you are, include your postal address, include a working unsubscribe, keep the subject line truthful
- **In plain English:** The United States does not require consent for commercial email, including business email, but every message must have truthful sender details and subject, clearly say it is an advertisement, show your valid physical postal address, and offer a free opt-out honoured within 10 business days. Never buy or harvest addresses through deception. This is not legal advice.
- **Checked on:** 2026-10-14
- **Sources:** https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/can-spam-act-compliance-guide-business
